I've been working this land for 40 years. My body knows what it needs and my land knows what I give it. I'm 64 now and farming alone, so I keep things simple and steady — I can't afford to experiment, and I don't need to.

My 4.1 mu runs the wheat-maize rotation, same as my neighbors, same as I've always done. Wheat goes in after the October harvest festivals, maize goes in as soon as I pull the wheat. The land doesn't rest — neither do I.

**Wheat:** I'll use the improved variety from the county seed station — not the old traditional seeds my mother used, those yields are too low. I apply compound fertilizer as base before planting, then urea topdress at jointing. I irrigate before winter sets in, again at jointing, and at heading — three times is enough with the well close by. I spray herbicide in early spring, and one fungicide pass for powdery mildew around heading time. My son-in-law helps me hire the rotary tiller and the combine — I can't run those machines myself anymore.

**Maize:** Hybrid seeds, same brand I've used for years from the village supply shop. After wheat harvest I'm in a hurry so I don't plow — I just let the machine direct-seed into the stubble. Two irrigations: one at emergence if it's dry, one at tasseling. One herbicide spray early, one insecticide for the corn borer. Maize doesn't need as much fussing as wheat.

I'm not going to change what works. My yields are consistent, my costs are known, and I know exactly how many bags of fertilizer to buy each season.
